classes.mechanism: Income (dividend, interest, reinvested distribution) earned on holdings the account kept until days earlier is credited on its pay date, after those holdings left. The form keeps income inside the return (dv, int and dvr are INTERNAL, flows:59/:62/:69) and divides the day's value change by the PRIOR DAY's value (returns:271), but the value carries no receivable for earned-not-yet-paid income, so the base is only what the exit left (cash on 113 of 119 days, a money-market fund on 6): a median 0.09 percent of the money that left in the prior 30 rows, against income of a median 0.05 percent of it. The money is real and is not an external flow (income is not in the flow table, flows:34-49); the daily number is not a return on any asset the account held that day.
classes.line: flows:59 (dv), :62 (int), :69 (dvr), :34-49 (EXTERNAL has no income type); returns:271 (prior-day base); daily_valuation:444 (value = quantity x price, no receivable)

classes.mechanism: A management-fee row (man) with a positive Amount is credited after the assets left: 42 of 43 are 'Fee Rebate <start> - <quarter end>' and one is a 'Fee Reversal' repeating two debits posted 14 months earlier. It refunds the unused part of an earlier quarterly debit: on 41 of the 42 days that have an earlier debit, the rebate over the account's last man debit equals the quarter fraction the note's period covers (+-0.02). The form took that debit as a DRAG (man: flows:86, :120-121; 0.05 percent of the then value) and takes the refund as a positive return on the residual cash left after the exit (returns:271), so a 0.05 percent drag is reversed by a day whose refund is 0.11 to 29.7 times the base. Right treatment: a refund of a drag belongs on the debit's base (or is left out of the day), not on the exit residual.
classes.line: flows:86 (man internal), :120-121 (man drag under the method); returns:271

classes.mechanism: No transaction explains the day: the account's whole value (one to thirteen positions, the largest 0.38 to 1.0 of the value) moved because the price series of its positions moved, and the series persists on the following days (no jump-and-revert): TSLA 2020-07-10, XOM 2020-11-09, NKE 2022-09-30 (down) and 2022-12-21, AAPL / AMZN / MSFT 2025-04-09 (a market-wide day: 91 percent of 1,201 priced securities up, median +7.7 percent), IBIT 2026-02-05 (down), NFLX 2026-02-27. The form's return is the value change and the value is quantity x close (daily_valuation:444).

A federal tax withholding row (ftax, two rows, CFNCASH) takes the whole remaining balance with no withdrawal (lo) the same day; the served rule (method_r28) counts a withholding as a flow only when a same-day lo rides it, so the money that left to the tax authority is no flow and the value goes to zero inside the return. method_r29 (a withholding is a flow with or without a lo) is written for exactly this and is not the rule of the served table. I did not run r29.
classes.line: flows:178 (R25_RIDING_WITHHOLDING, rides a lo only), :164 (WITHHOLDING_ALWAYS_FLOW_RULES = r29), :184-187 (r29 reason), :242-250 (withholding_flows)

classes.mechanism: A management-fee debit (man, negative) leaves a cash-only account: the value really fell by that fee (0.12 of the balance) and the method counts a fee as a drag inside the return (flows:120-121). The account was not emptied (295 rows remain) and the prior 30 rows carry an outflow of about the balance itself (1.04 times), so the base is the account's own cash, not the residual of a balance 100 times larger. A real, large cost; nothing in the form is wrong.

A ManAltT row (a management fee this account owes and another account pays) is not debited from this account's cash, so the form puts its Amount into the day's numerator (adj) while the value does not move: a fee of 0.36 of the balance, on a cash-only balance after an outflow 14.6 times its size in the prior 30 rows. It follows the written method (METHOD_DRAG_NO_CASH) by design; I class it FORM because the value is unchanged, the base is a residual and the cost is owed elsewhere.

A '12B1 ADJUSTMENT CREDIT' (type 12b1, positive; all 1,466 12b1 rows in the estate are positive credits) of 0.48 of the base is credited to the cash sweep after the account's value had been up to 58 times the prior value within the previous 60 rows (last above 5 times, 45 rows earlier); the form treats 12b1 as an internal fee credit (flows:85). Same shape as the fee refund (C2) with a different type; the account carries one 12b1 row.

Four holdings (CHPT, NIO, PLUG, FDRXX) are sold on the day; CHPT (15961R105) sells at 0.717 per share while the price store carries 14.48 for that day (14.66 the day before): 20.2 times the traded price, the size of a 1-for-20 reverse split applied backwards onto pre-split dates. The position is valued at 0.16 of the account on the prior day and its proceeds are 0.01, so value over prior is 0.85 from a price that is not the as-traded price. The store's own as_traded basis (price_basis.json) did not cover this CUSIP-date.
classes.line: daily_valuation:444 (value = quantity x store close); returns:271

classes.mechanism: The round-65 day. The first-day in-kind contribution (li, zero Amount) of CTVA (22052L104) is valued at the store close (11.34 per share) for both the holding and the flow (returns:143-152), so the first day reads 1.00 times the base; the next-day sale is at 76.16 per share, 6.63 times the store's 11.49, and the day's value over prior is 6.72. The store's CTVA series is 6.58 / 6.59 / 6.64 / 6.63 times below the traded price on every priced trade in the estate (2020Q3, 2024Q3, 2025Q2, 2026Q1): a constant scale, so the series, not this one close, is mis-scaled. The form worked as written (a zero-Amount in-kind is valued from the store) and passes the scale through; the INKIND_UNDERSTATED guard (returns:162) only tests a non-zero Amount.
classes.line: returns:143-152 (zero-Amount in-kind valued at the store close), :162 (_inkind_repair, non-zero Amount only); daily_valuation:444

evidence.rebuild: daily_returns.parquet (served table, cash_leg method_r28, run_commit 728d223d): 1,691,729 rows, 107,316 measured, 107,311 with a positive prior value; prior value 100.00 or more and abs(return) above 0.10 = 179, above 1.00 = 57, 0.10 to 1.00 = 122 (round 65's table: 179 / 57 / 122; no refusal).
evidence.method: Each day's return was decomposed from the account's own rows into the day's income (dv, dvlt, dvst, int, roy, ileu), man credits, man debits, tax rows, other fee rows and the price move of positions held both days (quantity x change in close). The parts reproduce the return to 0.01 on 176 of 179 days; the three others are the classes whose residual IS the cause (C6, C7, C8). A day is the rows between the prior row's date and the day, so a holiday transaction counts on the next trading day as the form does. read_row_by_row = transactions and holdings side by side for the day and the row before; hand_checked in a class = those days.

what_the_base_is.summary: Of the 162 days in classes C1 and C2 the prior-day base is cash only (CFNCASH / the bank sweep) on 154 and a single holding on 8 (the money-market fund FDRXX on 6 days, a GLD position sold the same day on 1, a fund of near-zero value on 1). In dollars the base is in the 100-1,000 band on 122 days, 1,000-10,000 on 38 and above 10,000 on 2, so 100.00 is not small; it is small against the account's own recent past: the money that left in the prior 30 rows is a median 1,000 times the base (base over outflow, median 0.0010; 152 of the 162 have 100 times or more, 161 have 10 times or more), and the income or the refund is a median 0.05 / 0.15 percent of that outflow.
what_the_base_is.what_it_was_left_by: A full withdrawal or in-kind transfer out (zero-Amount lo rows with a cash lo many times the base) in the days before; the base is then withdrawn by a later lo (a withdrawal of at least the base follows within 10 rows on 130 of the 162; the account's rows end within 10 rows on 111 of 162). On 22 of the 162 the prior row is itself blank NON_POSITIVE_BASE: the base is the previous day's first post-exit credit to a zero account. On 34 the prior row is also a day above 10 percent: a chain of post-exit credits.
what_the_base_is.dates: 123 of the 179 are dated 2026-05-20 to 2026-06-22 (105 of them to 2026-06-10): the accounts closed out in that window; the table ends 2026-06-22 and the last rows of such accounts are the credits.

c1_not_a_flow.entitlement_test: For each income row on a security the prior day did not hold, the amount per share (amount over the last quantity the account held) was compared with the per-share amount that other accounts holding it the day before received the same day. 213 rows have a peer sample. Equity / ETF / closed-end fund, 99 rows: 71 equal the peers' rate within 1 percent (the account was entitled to the full dividend and was paid after it left); 28 are not comparable (peer sample of 1 to 4 accounts, or a rate off by orders of magnitude) and are not established. Mutual fund, 114 rows: 93 are 0.30 to 0.95 of the peers' rate (a daily-accrual fund pays a leaver for the days held), 15 are zero-size, 6 not comparable. So the income is earned on the account's own earlier holdings, not put in from outside.
c1_not_a_flow.when_left: Rows since the income security was last held: median 7, range 2 to 18 (calendar days median 10, range 2 to 24).
c1_not_a_flow.sources: Dominant income source by day: equity / ETF / closed-end fund 80, mutual fund 34, bank-sweep interest 2 (credited after the sweep balance was withdrawn), money-market dividend 1, other 2. 117 of 119 days credit non-sweep income only on securities the prior day did not hold; the two others are one money-market fund still held at a fraction of its earlier size and one sweep-interest-only day.

c2_fee_refund.ratio_to_debit: Rebate over the last earlier man debit within 130 days: 42 of 43 have one; 41 of those 42 equal the quarter fraction the note's period covers within 0.02 (range 0.18 to 0.80; the period starts a median 44 days after the debit). The 43rd is a 'Fee Reversal' that repeats two debits posted 14 months earlier exactly (1.00 and 1.83 times the base).
c2_fee_refund.how_the_form_took_the_debit: As a drag inside the return (man internal, flows:86; drag under the method, flows:120-121). On the debit day it was 0.05 percent of the prior value (min, median and max equal at 4 decimals over the 42), the day's measured return 0.23 to 0.67 percent; the rebate over the base is 0.11 to 29.7, median 0.90.
c2_fee_refund.dates: 36 of 43 are dated 2026-05-22 or 2026-06-09; 42 of 43 notes begin 'Fee Rebate', the period starting a median 2.5 days before the credit.

c3_price_checks.cross_section: Share of priced securities moving by more than 10 percent on the day, and median move: 2025-04-09 28 percent, +7.7 percent (91 percent up); 2020-11-09 13 percent, +1.2 percent; 2026-02-05 2.2 percent, -0.9 percent; 2026-02-27 1.1 percent, -0.1 percent; 2020-07-10 0.9 percent; 2022-09-30 0.5 percent; 2022-12-21 0.2 percent.
c3_price_checks.trades: A trade price exists in the estate's transactions for three of the nine securities: AAPL on 2025-04-09 at 199.93 (store close 198.85); AMZN the day after at 184.82 (store 181.22); IBIT the day before at 42.86 (store 41.57).

round_65_form_day.day: Index 48 (2026-02-18), the one day of class C8; prior-value band 1k-10k, sign +, value over prior 6.72.
round_65_form_day.my_reading: On the first day of the account the in-kind contribution li (zero Amount) of CTVA is valued at the store close for the holding and for the flow, so value and flow are both 1.00 times the base; on 2026-02-18 the position is sold at 76.16 per share where the store's close is 11.49 (ratio 6.63); the day's value over prior is 6.72 (the sale proceeds over the store-valued holding).
round_65_form_day.agreement: I agree with the day, with the mechanism (a zero-Amount in-kind valued at a store close that the next-day sale contradicts) and with the size. I do not agree with the kind FORM: the store's CTVA closes are 6.58 / 6.59 / 6.64 / 6.63 times below the traded price on all four trades in the estate between 2020 and 2026, a constant scale of the whole series, so the cause is the price series (PRICE); the form's rule at returns:143-152 is applied as written. The field agrees_with_round_65_form_day is false for the kind only.

c4_c5_c7_days.c4: Index 2 (2014-12-03) and 25 (2020-11-13): both ftax on CFNCASH, no lo; the value goes to zero on both, so both have abs(return) of exactly 1.00 and sit in the 10 to 100 percent band (not above 1.00). On 25 the IRA close rows (fch, fco) are on the day too.
c4_c5_c7_days.c7: Index 43 (2025-05-23): CHPT store close 13.94 (05-19) to 14.66 (05-22) and 14.48 (05-23) against a sale at 0.717 on 05-23; the other three sold positions (NIO, PLUG, FDRXX) sold within 3 percent of their prior closes.
c4_c5_c7_days.c8_ratio_table: Median trade price over store price by quarter for CTVA: 2020Q3 6.58, 2024Q3 6.59, 2025Q2 6.64, 2026Q1 6.63 (one priced trade each; the 2019Q3 to 2020Q2 trades have no store price).

round_65_56_days.where_they_go: Round 65's record carries counts, not days (OUTLIER_DAYS.json has classes with counts only), so I match by count and cannot match by day. Its prior-value-100-or-more counts were A2 35, E 21, G 1 = 57; my 57 days above 1.00 are C1 35, C2 21, C8 1. The 56 'leftover balance' days are therefore FORM on a base that is cash after a close-out (C1 35: income paid after the holdings left; C2 21: a fee refund). Of the 56: cash-only base on 54, prior row blank NON_POSITIVE_BASE on 11, a withdrawal of at least the base within 10 rows on 55, rows ending within 10 rows on 43.
round_65_56_days.what_leftover_hides: 'Leftover balance' is true of the base against the account's recent past (a median 0.06 percent of the money that left) and false as a dollar size: 52 of the 56 sit in the 100-1,000 band and 4 in 1,000-10,000.

evidence.size_observation_for_the_threshold: Observation, not a ruling, and no rule was run: days whose prior 30 rows carry outflows of 100 times the prior value or more number 152, and all 152 are in classes C1 and C2; days with 10 times or more number 162, 161 in C1/C2 and 1 in C5b (the ManAltT day); none of the 10 TRUE_RETURN days, the 2 withholding days, the price-scale days or the 12b1 day has any such outflow. A prior value of 100.00 does not separate the classes (122 of the 162 C1/C2 days sit in the 100-1,000 band, and 1 other day, the 12b1 one, does); the base against the account's own outflow does.
day_index_columns: index (assigned, sorted by date then account)
evidence.privacy: No account id, dollar amount, quantity or per-account return is written; days are named by index.

not_established: Entitlement is shown by rate match for 71 of 99 equity-type income rows and by a daily-accrual fit for 93 of 114 mutual-fund rows; ex-dates and record dates were not read (no corporate-action source was used), so 'held on the record date' is inferred, not read. The 28 equity-type rows and 6 fund rows with no usable peer comparison are not established.

Why each account left (in-kind transfer out versus sale and withdrawal) was read only as zero-Amount lo rows plus a cash lo; the destination was not read, and the cause of the 2026-05-20 to 2026-06-10 window (a book of accounts closed or moved) is not established.

The right treatment of C1, C2 and C6 (accrue income, attribute the receipt to the exit day, net a refund against its debit, blank the day, or treat it as a flow) is a policy call; no rule was run on the table, so the effect of any rule on the 179 or on other days is not measured.
C4: method_r29 was not run; that it removes the two days rests on reading flows:242-250 and the days' types (ftax on CFNCASH, no lo).

C3: the 2026-02-05 IBIT and 2026-02-27 NFLX closes were checked only against the price store (persistence, cross-section) and, for IBIT, one trade the day before; no second price source was read. TRUE_RETURN there means the series is internally consistent, not verified externally. Of the nine securities only three have a trade price in the estate to compare with.

C8: that the CTVA series is on a back-adjusted scale (a corporate action) is consistent with a constant 6.6 factor but not established; whether other securities in the price store carry the same defect was not scanned. C7: that the CHPT close is a split-adjusted close is consistent with the 20.2 ratio and was not confirmed from a corporate-action source; why the as_traded re-derivation missed this CUSIP-date is not established.
Round 65's 56 days were matched to mine by count only (35 / 21 / 1); the day-level identity is unverified because its record has no day rows.

The prior-30-row outflow uses the table's flow column, which includes in-kind flows valued at the store close and is blank on FLOW_UNVALUED days; an exit whose flows were blank is under-counted. Peak-value ratios were not used because UNPRICED days hide the peak.

One pair of days (indexes 170 and 171, 2026-06-12) share a prior value to the cent and a return to five decimals with different transaction rows: related accounts, not examined. Other twin days (26/27, 28/29, 129/130 and the 2026-05-29 cluster) differ in the third decimal or more.

Class C5 (index 1, 2014-09-12) is called TRUE_RETURN because the value really fell by the fee; the fee's size against the cash (0.12) was not explained from a billing period (the 2014 note names none).
